title: The Unquiet Confession
premise: Retired detective Orsen Halloran, now barely keeping their bookshop afloat, is handed the diary of missing woman Elise Vann by her desperate sister. The entries continue for three weeks after Elise vanished, written in her hand, describing places only she could know — and naming Orsen as someone she trusted. As Orsen follows the diary's trail, they realize the killer is feeding them clues deliberately, someone who once worked beside them and knows every investigative habit they have. In the end, Orsen must choose between turning in the former partner who killed Elise to protect an old case's reputation, or burying the truth to protect the last loyalty they have left; they choose justice, recording the confession and letting the law take him, then finally closing the shop's back room where Elise's last entry waited all along.
about_author: Yara Lockridge is the pen name of a former small-town court reporter who spent a decade transcribing confessions before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Orsen Halloran's POV. Elise Vann's sister brings a diary whose final entries postdate the disappearance, and one names Orsen directly. Rereading old case notes at night, Orsen notices details in the diary that never appeared in any file — details only the investigators knew. Emotional beat: reluctant awakening, the pull of an unfinished case overriding a life deliberately built quiet.

chapters.title: The Hand That Writes Back
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, intercut with diary excerpts. Following the diary to locations Elise described, Orsen finds staged scenes arranged like evidence exhibits — someone is performing the case for them. A threatening note proves the killer anticipated each step. Emotional beat: dread curdling into obsession as Orsen realizes this is personal, a message meant for them alone.

chapters.title: What We Buried Together
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The trail leads to a closed case from Orsen's career, and to former partner Declan Reeve, who 'retired' the same month Elise began asking questions about it. Confronting Declan, Orsen hears half a confession wrapped in justifications of duty and protection. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief — the killer knows the file because he helped write it, and Orsen loved him like family.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Luring Declan to the bookshop with a forged diary page, Orsen records his full confession as he realizes too late he's been caught by his own methods. Police arrive on Orsen's anonymous tip; justice comes through the law Orsen chose over loyalty. Final beat: Orsen reads Elise's true last entry aloud alone, closes the book, and reopens the shop the next morning, changed but unbroken.
